features.name: Academic Preparation
features.description: Captures the level and strength of formal technical education the letter presents as preparation for the role.

levels.descriptor: No relevant degree or equivalent preparation is mentioned.
Mentions a bachelor's degree or equivalent.
Mentions a master's degree.
Mentions a doctoral degree.

features.name: Agentic Systems Architecture
features.description: Captures direct experience designing agent-based systems, especially their orchestration, guardrails, control boundaries, and supporting back-end infrastructure.

levels.descriptor: Gives no evidence of agentic-system design.
Mentions AI systems or automation without describing agent design.
Describes building agentic tooling with Python agents supported by backend services.
Explains concrete autonomy controls such as permissions, contracts, auditing, supervision, or bounded execution.

features.name: Algorithmic Fluency
features.description: Captures whether the letter demonstrates practical command of data structures and algorithms through concrete engineering improvements or redesigns.

levels.descriptor: No algorithmic strength is mentioned.
Algorithmic fluency is claimed, but without a concrete example.
At least one specific redesign or optimization shows applied algorithmic thinking.
Multiple or especially vivid examples show data structures and algorithms materially shaping system design.

features.name: Applied AI Production Maturity
features.description: Captures hands-on experience shipping AI or LLM-backed systems in production, especially with attention to reliability, evaluation, and failure modes.

levels.descriptor: No AI evidence.
Only vague, aspirational, or lightly specified AI mention.
Shows concrete experience shipping AI or LLM-backed functionality.
Shows concrete production AI work plus explicit evaluation, guardrails, correctness, or failure-mode management.

features.name: Collaboration and Learning Posture
features.description: Captures humility, coachability, and willingness to partner with security specialists or other internal stakeholders while growing security expertise.

levels.descriptor: No collaboration signal appears beyond applying for the role.
Cross-functional work is implied, but the posture toward security specialists is not explicit.
The letter explicitly shows enthusiasm for close collaboration with security engineers or learning from specialist teammates.

features.name: Developer Enablement Mindset
features.description: Captures whether the letter frames security engineering as helping developers and internal users act securely by default with lower friction, rather than policing them after the fact.

levels.descriptor: Does not discuss the needs or behavior of developer users.
Mentions helping teams in generic terms.
Explicitly focuses on reducing friction or making the secure path easier for developers.
Shows clear empathy for busy engineers and explains adoption in terms of defaults, workflows, and usable tooling rather than process.

features.name: Engineering Rigor
features.description: Captures the extent to which the letter emphasizes reliability, maintainability, correctness, testing, and careful operation in security-sensitive systems.

levels.descriptor: The letter gives little signal about quality, testing, reliability, or maintainability.
The letter gestures at seriousness or standards, but without concrete habits or practices.
The letter clearly emphasizes dependable systems, testing, maintainability, guardrails, or careful design.
The letter strongly signals security-critical rigor, with explicit habits such as typed or tested tooling, auditable boundaries, reliability-first design, or builder-quality standards.

features.name: Evidence Concreteness
features.description: Captures how concretely the letter substantiates claims with specific examples, mechanisms, scope, outcomes, or observable effects rather than generic assertions.

levels.descriptor: Mostly offers generic assertions or checklist-style requirement matching.
Provides some specifics, but major claims remain abstract or unsubstantiated.
Gives several concrete, role-relevant examples showing what was built or changed.
Repeatedly backs claims with precise mechanisms, context, and outcomes that make the applicant's contribution easy to picture.

features.name: Go Depth
features.description: Captures how strongly the letter establishes Go as a central, substantial production language in the applicant's experience.

levels.descriptor: No meaningful Go evidence.
Mentions Go, but without clear depth or ownership.
Shows regular production use of Go in recent work.
Makes Go clearly central, such as a principal language or daily driver tied to sustained backend ownership.

features.name: Narrative Cohesion and Voice
features.description: Captures whether the letter presents a memorable, well-structured, distinctive story or thesis rather than a formulaic checklist of qualifications.

levels.descriptor: The letter reads like an interchangeable template or a flat list of qualifications.
The letter is competent but generic, with limited individuality in framing or voice.
The letter has a distinctive opening, viewpoint, or sustained framing device.
The letter is memorable and cohesive, with a clear throughline linking the opening idea, past work, and motivation for this role.

features.name: Offensive Security Practice
features.description: Captures ongoing attacker-minded practice outside normal product work, especially through CTF participation or similar adversarial exercises.

levels.descriptor: No offensive-practice evidence is mentioned.
Mentions casual or occasional participation with little detail.
Shows regular participation presented as deliberate skill maintenance.
Shows strong results or serious competitive commitment that signals sustained offensive practice.

features.name: Open-Source Stewardship
features.description: Captures responsibility for public or upstream software through contribution, maintenance, releases, or fixing issues at the source for external users.

levels.descriptor: No open-source contribution or maintenance described.
Mentions occasional upstream patches or light contribution.
Shows active contribution or maintenance with review or release responsibility.
Maintains a used project or framework with sustained community, release, review, or user-support responsibilities.

features.name: Personal Project Ambition
features.description: Captures the ambition, technical rigor, and follow-through shown in self-directed projects outside formal job responsibilities.

levels.descriptor: No personal project is mentioned.
Mentions a small utility or simple side project with limited technical stretch.
Describes a substantial side project with nontrivial systems or reliability concerns.
Describes an ambitious systems project that tackles distributed systems, storage, recovery, consensus, or similarly hard engineering problems.

features.name: Platform Leverage Orientation
features.description: Captures motivation toward foundational infrastructure work whose benefits compound across many teams, products, or users.

levels.descriptor: Does not express a platform or foundational orientation.
Shows generic interest in scale or broad impact.
Explicitly values foundational work whose benefits spread across many teams.
Repeatedly frames contribution in terms of inherited improvements, central infrastructure, or organization-wide multipliers.

features.name: Production Software Experience
features.description: Captures the amount, breadth, and ownership of relevant professional experience building, launching, maintaining, and operating production software systems.

levels.descriptor: Meets the baseline only, with limited scope or a small number of launched systems described.
Shows a solid early-career record, with several years and some repeated launch or maintenance work.
Shows a strong mid-career record, with multiple launches and clear production breadth.
Presents an extensive record for this role, combining years, repeated launches, and broad responsibility across production systems.

features.name: Python Depth
features.description: Captures how convincingly the letter shows Python as a serious production language for services, tooling, automation, or related engineering work.

levels.descriptor: No Python evidence, or Python is only named without context.
Python is mentioned for basic scripting or generic use.
Shows substantial production Python use in services, automation, or internal tooling.
Shows deep production Python use with quality signals such as typed, tested, extensible, or central security tooling.

features.name: Role-Specific Motivation
features.description: Captures how specifically and persuasively the letter connects the applicant's background and goals to this exact role and its stated requirements.

levels.descriptor: Shows little role-specific motivation beyond wanting a software job or a brand-name employer.
Mentions security, scale, or Google in broad terms without a strong personal rationale.
Gives a clear role-relevant reason for interest, such as secure-by-default tooling or scaling scarce security effort.
Presents a precise, memorable thesis for wanting this role that is tightly tied to the team's mandate and the applicant's own priorities.

features.name: Security Assessment Practice
features.description: Captures hands-on experience reviewing systems, designs, or code for security weaknesses and following findings through remediation.

levels.descriptor: No assessment experience is shown.
Shows only general security interest or vocabulary without direct assessment work.
Shows direct experience performing security reviews or assessments.
Shows direct assessment experience plus method detail, such as threat models, attacker mindset, attack-surface mapping, or remediation verification.

features.name: Security Automation Insight
features.description: Captures how clearly the letter understands the role as a high-leverage security-automation problem of scaling security work through tooling, workflow design, and systems thinking.

levels.descriptor: Frames the role generically as software or security work, with little sign of understanding the specific problem the team solves.
Mentions automation or security scale in broad terms, but without a crisp diagnosis of the underlying bottleneck.
Frames the work as reducing manual security workload or improving vulnerability handling at scale.
Articulates a precise thesis about the domain, such as scaling scarce expert judgment, treating vulnerability response as a systems problem, or multiplying one finding into fleet-wide protection.

features.name: Security Credential Strength
features.description: Captures the presence, rigor, and relevance of formal external security certifications or other third-party security credentialing.

levels.descriptor: No relevant security certification is stated.
A baseline or survey credential such as Security+ is stated.
A rigorous hands-on credential such as OSCP or a similarly demanding practical certification is stated.

features.name: Security Engineering Philosophy
features.description: Captures whether the letter articulates a thoughtful, role-relevant point of view about what security engineering is for and why the work matters.

levels.descriptor: Little sign of a security-specific philosophy or perspective.
Expresses seriousness about security, but only in generic terms.
Shows a clear personal lens such as attacker thinking, builder's-eye reviewing, or preference for quiet resilience.
Presents a memorable, role-relevant philosophy that convincingly shapes how the applicant builds and evaluates systems.

features.name: Vulnerability Triage Automation
features.description: Captures direct experience building tooling that automates intake, triage, classification, routing, deduplication, or prioritization of vulnerability reports and related security-response workflows.

levels.descriptor: No past vulnerability-handling automation is mentioned.
The letter expresses interest in this problem, but gives no concrete example of having automated it.
A concrete example of triage, intake, routing, or report-handling automation is described.
The letter shows strong end-to-end automation of vulnerability handling, with clear workflow transformation or operational value.

features.name: Writing Polish
features.description: Captures the surface professionalism of the letter through proofreading, spelling, grammar, and copy-editing accuracy.

levels.descriptor: Frequent errors repeatedly interrupt reading or seriously undermine credibility.
Noticeable proofreading problems distract the reader more than once.
Contains some typos, but the letter remains easy to follow.
Mostly clean, with at most a minor slip.
Polished and effectively error-free at a professional standard.
